# Arithmetic cap interpolation with an exact peak deficit

This finite-source Brunn--Minkowski comparison is proved below. It
couples different parallel cap thresholds. It is not an OC theorem,
does not select a point, and does not add overlapping residue outputs.
the contributor proof; independent audit pending.

UPDATE: `candidate e7b862fa9bf72057` proves the
stronger bound (sum_i M_i/a_i-k+1)(sum_i lambda_i a_i^(1/d))^d by a
direct normalized layer-cake argument. It implies every bound here by
Hölder. In particular Section5's equation(9) is valid WITHOUT its balance
condition; that condition was needed only to derive it from the weaker
rearrangement formula. The proof and stated restricted implication here
remain correct, but use the stronger note for further numerical work.

## 1. Statement

Fix d>=1. For i=1,...,k let A_i be a finite union of compact convex
continuous fibers, with positive mixed d-volume M_i and largest fiber
volume a_i>0. Let lambda_i>0 with sum_i lambda_i=1. Suppose EVERY base
combination sum_i lambda_i p_i of positive-volume input fibers is an
integer point. Write T=sum_i lambda_i A_i, retaining at least these
positive-volume inputs. Its fibers are finite unions of convex compact
sets, and so have well-defined d-volume.

For arbitrary c_i in [0,1] satisfying sum_i c_i=k-1, one has

    mu(T) >= [ sum_i lambda_i^(d/(d+1))
                         (M_i-c_i a_i)^(1/(d+1)) ]^(d+1).    (1)

Zero-volume input fibers, if included in T as well, only enlarge it.
All input masses in this formulation are positive. A zero lambda is
omitted before choosing the c_i. For k=1, c_1=0 and (1) is equality.

For two midpoint inputs this becomes, for every 0<=c<=1,

    mu((A+B)/2) >= 2^(-d)
       [(M_A-c a)^(1/(d+1))
          +(M_B-(1-c)b)^(1/(d+1))]^(d+1).             (2)

The bases of A and B in one common parity class ensure the needed
integrality. More generally lambda_i=j_i/m with positive integers j_i
summing to m works when all bases lie in one residue class modulo m.

## 2. An auxiliary count rearrangement

Let a source have positive fiber volumes v_1>=...>=v_N>0. Let omega_d
be the volume of the unit Euclidean ball in R^d. For 0<=c<=1 define
the compact set in the AUXILIARY space R times R^d

    R_c(A)=union_(j=1)^N
       [-(j-c)/2,(j-c)/2] times
                    ((v_j/omega_d)^(1/d) B_d).       (3)

Its (d+1)-volume is exactly

    |R_c(A)|=M-c a.                                  (4)

Indeed at an x with omega_d |x|^d=t its horizontal interval has length
N_A(t)-c, where N_A(t) counts fibers with volume at least t, as long
N_A(t)>0. Polar integration changes the radial volume coordinate to dt,
and gives integral_0^a(N_A(t)-c)dt. The finitely many threshold equalities
do not affect this integral.

The CLOSED interval convention in (3) is essential at c=1: a one-fiber
source then gives a nonempty d-dimensional ball of zero (d+1)-volume.
It is not replaced by the empty set. Ordinary Brunn--Minkowski for
nonempty compact measurable sets still applies when some such volumes
vanish. No convexity of the union (3) is asserted or needed.

## 3. A sumset inclusion without collision overcounting

If finite nonempty sets P_1,...,P_k lie in a real vector space, then

    |P_1+...+P_k| >= sum_i |P_i|-k+1.                (5)

For two sets, order each by a common linear functional that is injective
on each. The list p_min+q_1,...,p_min+q_N followed by
p_2+q_max,...,p_M+q_max is strictly increasing and has M+N-1 members.
Apply this repeatedly, choosing a generic functional at each stage if
necessary, to prove (5). Multiplication of a set by a positive scalar
does not change its cardinality.

Let L_i(s,x)=(s,lambda_i x). We claim the exact set inclusion

    sum_i L_i R_(c_i)(A_i) subset R_0(T).             (6)

For a point (s_i,x_i) in the i-th summand let P_i consist of the input
bases with fiber volume at least omega_d |x_i|^d, retaining only the
positive-volume bases. It is nonempty, and write its size N_i. The
definition (3) gives |s_i|<=(N_i-c_i)/2.

For every choice p_i in P_i, the output fiber at sum_i lambda_i p_i
contains the Minkowski combination of the respective convex fibers.
Ordinary d-dimensional Brunn--Minkowski gives its volume at least

    (sum_i lambda_i v_(i,p_i)^(1/d))^d
       >= omega_d (sum_i lambda_i |x_i|)^d
       >= omega_d |sum_i lambda_i x_i|^d.            (7)

These outputs are integer bases by the stated hypothesis. By (5) there
are at least sum_i N_i-k+1 DISTINCT such bases. On the other hand,

    |sum_i s_i| <= (sum_i N_i-sum_i c_i)/2
                 =(sum_i N_i-k+1)/2.

This is exactly the horizontal-width criterion for membership in the
right side of (6), at continuous coordinate sum_i lambda_i x_i. The
zero radius case causes no problem: the chosen inputs all have positive
volumes, and their positive-weight Minkowski sums have positive volume.
Thus (6) includes the endpoints of the cylinders as claimed.

Taking (d+1)-volumes in (6), applying ordinary Brunn--Minkowski to the
nonempty compact sets L_i R_(c_i)(A_i), and using

    |L_i R_(c_i)(A_i)|=lambda_i^d(M_i-c_i a_i)

proves (1). The linear maps here act ONLY on the auxiliary rearrangements.
Their determinant factors are displayed explicitly. They are not changes
of the original mixed-integer lattice or its measure.

## 4. Parallel oblique cap profiles

Take A_i to be the positive-volume fibers in a fixed residue class of

    C intersect {ell>=t_i},

where ell is any affine functional on the full ambient space. Whenever
the base-combination integrality condition holds, convexity gives

    sum_i lambda_i A_i
        subset C intersect {ell>=sum_i lambda_i t_i}.

Consequently (1) is a lower bound on the ACTUAL mixed mass of that
interpolated cap. All integer and continuous coefficients of ell are
allowed. The halfspaces are closed; no boundary mass is dropped. If
one input cap has zero mixed mass, (1) as stated is not applied to it.

The rearrangements are used solely to prove a numerical mass comparison.
They do not assert a relation between maximal halfspace depths of the
original source and a rearranged source.

## 5. Exact consequences and sharp examples

For k=m identical inputs, lambda_i=1/m and c_i=1-1/m, formula (1) gives

    mu((A+...+A)/m) >= m M-(m-1)a.                  (8)

For a single positive fiber in each input, write r_i=a_i^(1/d), and
choose 1-c_i=lambda_i r_i/(sum_j lambda_j r_j). These numbers sum to
one, so the c_i are admissible. Direct substitution in (1) gives the
ordinary sharp fiber inequality

    mu(T)>=(sum_i lambda_i a_i^(1/d))^d.

For two midpoint inputs put R_A=M_A/a, R_B=M_B/b, A=a^(1/d), B=b^(1/d),
and R=R_A+R_B-1. If

    c_*=R_A-R A/(A+B) belongs to [0,1],

substitution of c_* into (2) gives the stronger convenient form

    mu((A_source+B_source)/2) >= R ((A+B)/2)^d.      (9)

Here the capital scalar A is distinct from the source A_source.
The chosen c_* makes R_A-c_*=R A/(A+B) and
R_B-1+c_*=R B/(A+B), which verifies (9) algebraically. Differentiation
also shows c_* maximizes (2) when it is in this interval. If it is
outside, (9) is NOT inferred; (2) remains valid for every admissible c.

For an explicit sharp comparison let d=2 and choose a convex body K of
area one. Take A_source={0,2} times 2K and
B_source={0,2,4} times 3K. Then M_A=8, a=4, M_B=27, b=9,
c_*=2/5, R=4. The output has bases0,1,2,3, each with fiber (5/2)K,
so its mass is exactly25, the right side of (9). The earlier bound
max(R_A,R_B)((A+B)/2)^d gives only75/4 here. Both inequalities are
valid; the new one captures additional distinct output bases.

The bound in (2) need not dominate that earlier maximum-ratio bound
for every input. They may be used together by taking their maximum.
Neither may be summed over different residue classes whose outputs
overlap. Although (1) now connects different cap thresholds, there is
still no proved all-direction deterministic-center step yielding OC.
